language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

Hi, my name is Colette! Welcome aboard and meet my friend Tim. Join us on our trip while we sail through different experiences. All hands on
deck, ahoy!
Hey, there! I hope you too are looking forward to this exciting journey!
Tim and I love to explore new places and learn new things. Today, we plan to visit the Alexandrian Lighthouse. We are currently passing a canal and will reach the lighthouse in a few hours.
Other than travelling, I also love to read, especially books on science. My favorite subject is Chemistry. I have a book on Chemistry down in the cabin. Come let’s explore it together.
That's a great idea, Colette. You can also complete your school assignment. Let's go!

The chemistry book I am reading, is about mixtures. A mixture is a combination of two or more substances with no chemical reaction taking place between the components. An other characteristic of the components of a mixture is that you can separate them.
When the components have undergone a chemical reaction, this cannot be reversed nor can the substances be separated anymore. Then it's not a mixture anymore.
I would really like to practice with identifying mixtures. Will you help me? Let's sort the mixtures and compounds by dragging each item into the correct drop area.

Do you know what a homogeneous mixture is? It is a mixture in which the composition is uniform. You can't see the different ingredients of the mixture. Can you help me find the
homogeneous mixtures?
Yes Colette! For example, a mixture of water and sugar!
See, I have a lot of pictures on this table. Can you help me pin the pictures of homogeneous mixtures on the cork board? All you need to do is click the correct picture.

outro.text: Wow! We did manage to get this picture board in place. Thanks a lot for your help. I will give this board to my teacher so she can showcase it in our Chemistry lab!

I'm hungry! Luckily the captain said that dinner arrives in a few minutes. While we wait for the food, let's talk about heterogeneous mixtures, which are just the opposite of homogeneous mixtures. They contain physically distinct parts and have non-uniform compositions.
See, we have some food items on the dining table. Can you please help me identify if these mixtures are heterogeneous or not?
